newsitem.title: USA: Lyondell-Citgo refining upgrade ahead of schedule.
newsitem.headline: Lyondell-Citgo refining upgrade ahead of schedule.

text.p: Lyondell Petrochemical Co said Monday the upgrade project at Lyondell-Citgo Refining Co Ltd was in service as of March 1, one month ahead of schedule.

The $1.1 billion project, which began in 1994, upgraded the refinery's ability to process very heavy crude oil from Venezuela. The upgrade will stabilize and improve earnings and cash flows, making venture more profitable for its owners, Lyondell and Citgo Petroleum Corp, a subsidiary of Petroleos de Venezuela, the national oil company of Venezuela.

With the completion of the upgrade project, Lyondell-Citgo Refining is one of the nation's most complex refineries, able to process more than 215,000 barrels per day of very heavy crude oil in a full conversion mode, Lyondell said.

The agreement that formed the venture includes a long-term crude oil supply contract with PDVSA to supply Lyondell-Citgo Refining with up to 230,000 barrels per day of very heavy (17 degree gravity) crude oil.
The company said this provides the refinery with a secure and consistent supply of heavy crude oil with a stable profit margin.
As part of the venture agreements, Citgo purchases and markets most of the refined product output from LCR.

"While the next few months will likely involve typical start-up and optimization issues," Lyondell chief executive Dan F. Smith said, the company "expects to enjoy significantly increased benefits from enhanced and stabilized earnings and cash flow from the refinery in the second half of the year."
With the upgrade complete, Lyondell has an about 60 percent participation interest in the venture, and Citgo has the remaining interest.

"From the very beginning, the products provided by the joint venture project have enhanced Citgo's growth capabilities in Midwest markets while fulfilling one of our major goals of assisting our parent company, PDVSA, in securing guaranteed, long-term markets for Venezuela's heavy crude oil," Citgo cief executive Ralph S. Cunningham said.

Lyondell noted the upgrade was not designed to increase total crude oil throughput of the refinery, but rather to enable it to process heavier crude oil and produce higher valued products such as reformulated gasoline and low-sulfur diesel.

Major components of the upgrade project included new crude oil distillation, delayed coking, hydrotreating and sulfur recovery units. In connection with the upgrade, modifications were completed on the site's largest distillation unit, three hydrotreaters and two sulfur recovery units.
